Given such a pair $(i_C:C\to X, h\in {\mathcal O}_{C: C\cap X^*}^\times)$, let  $(C\cap X^*)_U=(C\cap X^*)\cap U$, write the finite set $C\cap X^*$ as a disjoint union
\[
C\cap X^*=(C\cap X^*)_U\amalg B,
\]
and let $V= (X\setminus X^*)\cup U$. Then $B\subset X(d)\setminus (S\cup T)=X(d)^0\setminus S$ and $V$ is an open neighborhood of $C^0:=C\setminus B$ in $X(d)$. Moreover, $f$ is flat over $V$.  

Let $C_Y^0=f^{-1}(C^0)\subset f^{-1}(V)$ and let $C_Y\subset Y$ be the closure of $C_Y^0$ in $Y$. Since $f_C$ is flat of relative dimension zero  over $C\cap V$, $C_Y$ is a pure dimension one closed subscheme of $f^{-1}(C)$, and $f$ restricts to a quasi-finite morphism $f_C:C_Y\to C$. We also have the flat quasi-finite morphism $f_{C^0}:C_Y^0\to C^0$. Let $h_{C_Y}$ be the rational function $f_C^*(h)$ on $C_Y$ and 
$h_{C^0_Y}$ the rational function $f_{C^0}^*(h)$ on $C_Y^0$. Let $i_{C_Y}:C_Y\to Y$, $i_{C^0_Y}:C^0_Y\to f^{-1}(V)$ be the respective closed immersions.

 Note that $(C_Y\setminus C_Y^0)\cap f^{-1}(U)=\0$, so $C_Y\cap Y^*\subset f^{-1}(C\cap U)$. As $f$ is  flat over $U$ and $Y^*\subset f^{-1}(X^*)$, this implies that $C_Y\cap Y^*$ is a finite set and that $C_Y$ is defined by a regular sequence in a neighborhood of $C_Y\cap Y^*$ in $Y$. Thus $C_Y$ is a Cartier curve on $Y$ relative to $Y^*$.   Moreover,    $h_{C_Y}$ is in ${\mathcal O}_{C_Y: C_Y\cap Y^*}^\times$ since $h\in {\mathcal O}_{C: C\cap X^*}^\times$. Since $h$ is a unit in ${\mathcal O}_{C, B}$, it follows that $h_{C_Y}$ is also a unit in ${\mathcal O}_{C_Y, C_Y\cap f^{-1}(B)}$ so
\[
{\operatorname{div}}_{C_Y}(h_C)={\operatorname{div}}_{C^0_Y}(h_C^0)\in Z_0(C_Y).
\]


Let $f_V:f^{-1}(V)\to V$ be the restriction of $f$, and let $i_{C\cap V}:C\cap V\to V$, $i_{C_Y^0}:C_Y^0\to f^{-1}(V)$ be the inclusions. As $f_V$ is flat,  we have
\[
f_V^*(i_{C\cap V*})({\operatorname{div}} h|_{C\cap V}))=i_{C^0_Y*}({\operatorname{div}} h_{C_Y^0})
\]
by standard results of classical intersection theory (see, e.g., \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02S1}{Tag 02S1}]{stacks-project}). Thus
\[
f^*(i_{C*}({\operatorname{div}} h))=
f_V^*(i_{C\cap V*}({\operatorname{div}} h|_{C\cap V}))=i_{C^0_Y*}({\operatorname{div}} h_{C_Y^0})=
i_{C_Y*}({\operatorname{div}} h_{C_Y}). 
\]
Thus $f^*:Z^d(X\setminus X^*)\to Z^d(Y\setminus Y^*)$ satisfies
\[
f^*(R^d(X, X^*))\subset R^d(Y, Y^*),
\]
and therefore $f^*$ descends uniquely to a map
\[
f^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)
\]
on the  quotients.

Given a second  admissible pair $(Z, Z^*)$, a subset $S'\subset Y^*$ and morphism $g:Z\to Y$ satisfying (i)-(iii), we have the pullback map $g^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Z, Z^*)$. We first check that $(fg)^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Z, Z^*)$ is also defined.

The condition (i) for $fg$ follows directly from (i) for $f$ and for $g$. Next, by (ii),  $f:Y\to X$ is flat over $X\setminus X^*$ and $g:Z\to Y$ is flat over $Y\setminus Y^*$. Since $Y\setminus Y^*\supset f^{-1}(X\setminus X^*)$, it follows that $fg$ is flat over $X\setminus X^*$.

Let  $S\subset X^*\cap X(d)$ be a closed subset  and  $U\subset X$ an open neighborhood of  $f(Y^*)\cap X(d)^0\setminus S$ in $X(d)^0$  satisfying (iii) for $f$, and let  $S'\subset Y^*\cap Y(d)$, $U'\subset Y$ be given similarly for $g$. Let $\overline{f(S')}\subset X^*$ be the closure of $f(S')$ and let $S''=S\cup \overline{f(S')}$. Since $g(Z^*)\subset Y^*$, we have $fg(Z^*)\subset f(Y^*)$ and it is then easy to see that $S''$ and $U'':=U$ satisfy (iii) for $fg$ and hence $(fg)^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Z, Z^*)$ is defined.

The functoriality for flat pullback
\[
(fg)^*=g^*f^*:Z^d(X\setminus X^*)\to Z^d(Z\setminus Z^*)
\]
on the level of cycles then implies
\[
(fg)^*=g^*f^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Z, Z^*). 
\]
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
\label{rem:OpenIm} 1. We may apply Lemma~\ref{lem:EtalePullback} to the case of an open immersion $j:U\to X$, with ${\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kU=d$, taking $S=\0$, to give a well-defined restriction map
\[
j^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X,X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(U,U\cap X^*),
\]
functorial for open immersions.\\[2pt]
2. We may also apply Lemma~\ref{lem:EtalePullback} to the case of a morphism $f:Y\to X$, with $Y$  regular and of pure dimension $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$ over $k$ and $f:Y\to X$ flat over $X\setminus X^*$, where we take $Y^*=S=U=\0$. The gives the well-defined pullback map
\[
f^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y),
\]
satisfying $(fg)^*=g^*f^*$ for flat morphisms $g:Z\to Y$ in ${\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}^{\operatorname{\text{\rm qp}}}_k$ with $Z$ regular and of pure dimension $d$.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:base-change} Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair over $k$, let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$, and let $k\hookrightarrow F$ be an extension of fields. Let $X_F=X\times_kF$ with projection $p_X:X_F\to X$ and let $X_F^*=p_X^{-1}(X^*)$. Suppose that $X_F(d)^0$ is reduced and $X_F\setminus X_F^*$ is regular. Then\\[5pt]
1. $(X_F, X_F^*)$ is an admissible pair over $F$ and ${\operatorname{\rm dim}}_FX_F={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$.\\[2pt]
2. Flat pullback for the restriction $p_X:X_F\setminus X_F^*\to X_F\setminus X_F^*$ gives a well-defined map $p_X^*:Z^d(X\setminus X^*)\to Z^d(X_F\setminus X_F^*)$, which descends to $p_X^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X_F, X_F^*)$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
For $Z\in {\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}_k$ let $Z_F:=Z\times_kF$. We have ${\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kZ={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_FZ_F$, so in particular $X_F(i)=X(i)_{F, {\rm red}}$ for all $i$ and  ${\operatorname{\rm dim}}_FX_F={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX=d$. Thus $X_F^*\supset X_F(i)$ for all $i<d$. Since $X_F(d)^0$ is reduced and $X_F\setminus X_F^*$ is regular by assumption, $(X_F, X_F^*)$ is thus an admissible pair, which proves (1).

For (2), $p_X:X_F\to X$ is flat and thus $p_X:X_F\setminus X_F^*\to X_F\setminus X_F^*$ is flat and we have the well-defined pullback $p_X^*:Z^d(X\setminus X^*)\to Z^d(X_F\setminus X_F^*)$. If $i_C:C\to X$ is a Cartier curve on $X$ relative to $X^*$, then $C_{\rm red}$ is a  closed subscheme of $X(d)$ of pure codimension $d-1$, so the base-change $C_F$ has support  a closed subset of $X_F(d)$ of pure codimension $d-1$. Thus $i_{C_F}:C_F\to X_F$ has pure dimension one and is supported in $X_F(d)$. Similarly, $C_F\cap X_F^*$ is the finite set of points $p_X^{-1}(C\cap X^*)$, and by flatness, the fact that $C$ is a complete intersection on $X$ in a neighborhood of $C\cap X^*$ implies that $C_F$ is a complete intersection on $X_F$ in a neighborhood of $C_F\cap X_F^*$, that is, $i_{C_F}:C_F\to X_F$ is a Cartier curve on $X_F$ relative to $X_F^*$. Finally, if we have $f\in {\mathcal O}_{C: C\cap X^*}^\times$, then letting $p_C:C_F\to C$ be the restriction of $p_X$, we have $p_C^*(f)\in {\mathcal O}_{C_F: C_F\cap Y^*}^\times$ and
\[
i_{C_F*}({\operatorname{div}} p_C^*(f))=p_X^*(i_{C*}({\operatorname{div}} f)),
\]
so $p^*(R^d(X, X^*))\subset R^d(X_F, X_F^*)$.  Thus  $p_X^*:Z^d(X, X^*)\to Z^d(X_F, X_F^*)$ descends to $p_X^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X_F, X_F^*)$, proving (2).
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
In case $k$ is perfect, or more generally, if $F$ is separable over $k$, the assumptions on $X_F(d)^0$ and $X_F\setminus X_F^*$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:base-change} are automatically satisfied.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:Localization} Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair, let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$ and let $i:W\to X$ be a closed immersion, with $i(W)\subset X\setminus X^*$. Then the pushforward $i_*:Z_0(W)\to Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$ descends to a group homomorphism 
\[
i_*:{\operatorname{CH}}_0(W)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X,X^*)
\]
Moreover, letting $U:=X\setminus W$ with open immersion $j:U\to X$, $(U, X^*)$ is an admissible pair, and the sequence
\begin{equation}\label{eqn:Localization}
{\operatorname{CH}}_0(W)\xrightarrow{i_*}{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X,X^*)\xrightarrow{j^*}{\operatorname{CH}}^d(U,X^*)\to 0
\end{equation}
is exact.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
It is clear that for $C\subset W$ an integral curve, $i(C)\subset X$ is a Cartier curve relative to $X^*$, and for $h\in k(C)^\times$, $i_*(i_{C*}({\operatorname{div}} h))$ is in $R^d(X,X^*)$. This shows that $i_*:Z_0(W)\to Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$ descends to $i_*:{\operatorname{CH}}_0(W)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X,X^*)$.

The proof of the exactness of the sequence \eqref{eqn:Localization} is exactly the same as for the usual Chow groups:  The sequence
\[
0\to Z_0(W)\xrightarrow{i_*}Z^d(X\setminus X^*)\xrightarrow{j^*}Z^d(U\setminus X^*)\to 0
\]
is exact, and if $C_U$ is a Cartier curve on $U$ relative to $X^*$, with $h\in {\mathcal O}_{C_U:C_U\cap X^*}^\times$, then since $U\cap X^*=X^*$, we see that the closure $C$ of $C_U$ in $X$  is a Cartier curve on $X$ relative to $X^*$, $h$ determines a unique rational function $h_C\in {\mathcal O}_{C: C\cap X^*}^\times$ on $C$, and if $z\in Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$ has $j^*(z)=i_{C_U*}({\operatorname{div}}  h)$, then $z-i_{C*}({\operatorname{div}} h_C)=i_*(w)$ for a unique $w\in Z_0(W)$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:PartialFunct} Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair. Take $z, z'\in Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$, let $i_C:C\to X$ be a Cartier curve on $X$ relative to $X^*$ and take $h\in {\mathcal O}_{C:C\cap X^*}^\times$ with $i_{C*}({\operatorname{div}} h)=z-z'$. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of quasi-projective varieties over $k$, and suppose that $Y$ is reduced, of pure dimension $d:={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$ over $k$, and that there is an open subscheme $U$ of $X\setminus X^*$ such that, letting $V=f^{-1}(U)$ and $f_U:V\to U$ the restriction of $f$, we have\\[5pt]
i. $f_U:V\to U$ is flat\\[2pt]
ii. $U$ contains ${\rm supp}\,(z)\cup {\rm supp}\,(z')$, all closed points $p$ of $C$ such that $f$ is not a unit in ${\mathcal O}_{C,p}$ and all generic points of $C$.
\\[5pt]
Let $f_{U\cap C}:f_U^{-1}(C\cap U)\to C\cap U$ be the restriction of $f_U$ and let  $D$ be the closure in $Y$ of $f_U^{-1}(C\cap U)$. Then $f_{U\cap C}$ is quasi-finite, so we have the well-defined rational function $f_{U\cap C}^*(h)$ on $f_U^{-1}(C\cap U)$ 

Let $f^*(h)\in k(D)^*$ be the rational function with $f^*(h)_{|f_U^{-1}(C\cap U)}=f_{U\cap C}^*(h)$. Then $f^*(z)$ and $f^*(z')$ are defined as cycles, and 
\[
f^*(z)-f^*(z')=i_{D*}({\operatorname{div}}(f^*(h)))
\]
In particular, $f^*(z-z')=0$ in ${\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y)$.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
$D$ is clearly a closed subscheme of the closed subscheme $f^{-1}(C)$ of $Y$, so the restriction of $f$ to $D$ defines a quasi-finite morphism $f_D:D\to C$. Thus  $f^*_D(h)$ is a well-defined  rational function on $D$, with $f^*_D(h)$ equal to $f_{U\cap C}^*(h_{| U\cap C})$ on $f_U^{-1}(C\cap U)$, so $f_D^*(h)=f^*(h)$. In addition, at each point $p$ of $D\setminus f^{-1}(U\cap C)$, $h$ is in ${\mathcal O}_{C, f(p)}^\times$, so $f^*(h)$ is a unit in ${\mathcal O}_{D, p}$, and thus ${\operatorname{div}}(f^*(h))$ is supported on $f^{-1}(U\cap C)$. Since 
\[
f^*(z)-f^*(z')=i_{f^{-1}(U\cap C)*}({\operatorname{div}} f_{U\cap C}^*(h))
\]
by \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02S1}{Tag 02S1}]{stacks-project}, we see that
\[
f^*(z)-f^*(z')=i_{D*}({\operatorname{div}}(f^*(h))).
\]
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
1. Let $G$ be a linear algebraic group over $k$, i.e., $G$ is a group-scheme over $k$ that admits a description as a closed subgroup scheme of $\operatorname{GL}_n/k$ for some $n$. Recall that $G$ is called {\em $k$-rational} if $G$ is smooth over $k$, geometrically connected, and there is a dense open subscheme $U$ of $G$ that is isomorphic to an open dense subscheme in a projective space ${\mathbb P}^{{\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kG}_k$ over $k$. A $k$-rational linear algebraic group $G$ over $k$ is called {\em strongly $k$-rational} if given dense open subschemes $U, V\subset G$, we have $U(k)*V(k)=(U*V)(k)$.\\[5pt]
2. Let $G$ be a linear algebraic group over $k$. For us a {\em homogeneous space}  for $G$ is a smooth, finite-type $k$-scheme $H$ with $H(k)\neq\0$, endowed with a $G$-action $\rho:G\times_kH\to H$ such that, for $x\in H(k)$, the isotropy subgroup $G_x$ is a reduced subgroup-scheme of $G$ and the action map $\rho_x:G=G\times_kx\to H$, $\rho_x(g)=g\cdot x$, identifies $H$ with the quotient $G/G_x$.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- remarks-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:Star} 1. Our definition of the term ``homogeneous space'' is non-standard in positive characteristic, in that we require smoothness over $k$ and the isotropy group $G_x$ to be reduced for each $k$-point $x$, but we use it to avoid encumbering the notation with additional adjectives. In our applications, $G$ will always be a product of general linear groups, and $H$ with always be a product of Grassmannians or flag varieties, which does satisfy our additional requirements.\\[5pt]
2. Let $G$ be a $k$-rational linear algebraic group over $k$ that satisfies Hilbert's Theorem 90 over $k$, that is, $H^1_\text{\'et}(k, G)=\{*\}$. Then $G$ is strongly $k$-rational. Indeed, letting $\mu:G\times G\to G$ be the multiplication map, then for $x\in G(k)$, the fiber $\mu^{-1}(x)$ is a torsor for $G$ over ${\rm Spec\,} k$, $G$ acting by $g\cdot (y,z):=(yg^{-1}, gz)$. Thus $\mu^{-1}(x)\cong G$ as $k$-scheme, and in particular, every dense open subscheme $U$ of $\mu^{-1}(x)$ has $U(k)$ Zariski dense in $U$. We apply this to $A, B$ dense open subsets of $G$, $x\in (A*B)(k)$ and $U=A\times B\cap \mu^{-1}(x)$, which gives us a point $(a,b)\in A(k)\times B(k)$ with $\mu(a,b)=x$, showing $G$ is strongly $k$-rational.
<!-- end remarks-1 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
Let $Z$ be a quasi-projective $k$-scheme, and let $A, B\subset Z$ be closed subsets. We say that $A$ and $B$ intersect properly in $Z$ if for each point $z\in A\cap B$ we have
\[
{\operatorname{\rm dim}}_k(A\cap B, z)={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_k(A,z)+{\operatorname{\rm dim}}_k(B,z)-{\operatorname{\rm dim}}_k(Z,z).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
{\rm codim}_Z(A\cap B, z)={\rm codim}_Z(A,z)+{\rm codim}_Z(B,z).
\]
Note that $A$ and $B$ intersect properly if $A\cap B=\0$.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
\label{rem:lci}
For $i:W\to Z$ a closed immersion in ${\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}_k$, the subset 
\[
W_{\operatorname{lci}}:=\{w\in W\mid {\mathcal I}_{W,w}\subset {\mathcal O}_{Z,w}\text{ is generated by a regular sequence}\}
\]
is open in $W$ and is equal to the maximal open subscheme $U$ of $W$ such that $U\to Z$ is a regular immersion (see, e.g., \cite[Proposition 16.9.10]{EGAIV4} or \cite[Lemma 31.21.8(1,5)\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/063I}{Tag 063I}]{stacks-project}).
Let $W_{\operatorname{nlci}}:=W\setminus W_{\operatorname{lci}}$.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:TranslateCycle} Let $G$ be a $k$-rational linear algebraic group, $H$ a homogeneous space for $G$. Take $Z\in {\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}_k$, let   $f :Z\to H$ be a morphism, and let $Y$ be a reduced closed subscheme of $H$ of
pure codimension $i$. Let $Z^*\subset Z$ be a closed subset with ${\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kZ^*<{\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kZ$ and let $Z_0\subset Z$ be a closed subset of dimension $<i$. Then there is a dense open subset $O(f , Y, Z^*, Z_0)\subset G$ such that for each
$g \in O(f, Y, Z^*, Z_0)(k)$, the following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item  $f^{-1}(gY)$ has pure codimension $i$ in $Z$.
\item  $f^{-1}(gY)$ intersects $Z^*$  properly in $Z$ and $f^{-1}(gY)\cap Z_0=\0$.
\item $f^{-1} (gY)$ is a local complete intersection in $Z$ at each generic point of
$f^{-1}(gY)\cap Z^*$.
\item  The sheaves ${\operatorname{\rm Tor}}^{{\mathcal O}_H}_i({\mathcal O}_{gY}, {\mathcal O}_Z) $ vanish for all $i>0$, that is, ${\mathcal O}_{gY}$ and ${\mathcal O}_Z$ are Tor-independent over ${\mathcal O}_H$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, $O(f,Y, Z^*, Z_0)(k)$ is Zariski dense in $O(f,Y, Z^*, Z_0)$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
This is a version of Kleiman's transversality theorem \cite[Theorem 2]{Kleiman}. The case of   $k$ to be algebraically closed, with minor changes in the statement,  is \cite[Lemma 4]{BS98} and the result in general follows easily from the case of algebraically closed $k$, as we now explain. 

 Let $k\to \bar{k}$ be an algebraic closure. (1) and (2) follow directly from the case of algebraically closed $k$, since given a dense open subset $V\subset G$ such that (1) and (2) are satisfied for all $g\in V(\bar{k})$, the fact that $G$ is $k$-rational implies that $V(k)$ is dense in $V$, and we can consider each $k$-point of $V$ as a $\bar{k}$-point.

 (4) follows similarly from the algebraically closed case, using the fact that $k\to \bar{k}$ is faithfully flat, so we can deduce the vanishing of the Tor-sheaves from their vanishing after base-extension by $k\to \bar{k}$. 
 
 For (3),   since $H$ is smooth over $k$,  the local ring ${\mathcal O}_{H,x}$  a regular local ring for all $x\in H$ \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/056S}{tag 056S}]{stacks-project}. In particular, for each generic point $y$ of $Y$, 
 the local ring ${\mathcal O}_{H, y}$ is a regular local ring, of dimension $i$, so the maximal ideal is generated by a regular sequence of length $i$ and as $Y$ is reduced, it follows that $y$ is in $Y_{\operatorname{lci}}$. Following Remark~\ref{rem:lci},  $Y_{\operatorname{lci}}$ is open and dense in $Y$. Thus,  there is an affine open subset $U={\rm Spec\,} A\subset H$ with $U\cap Y$ dense in $Y$, such that the ideal $I\subset A$ of the closed subscheme $Y\cap U$ of $U$ is generated by a regular sequence $s_1,\ldots, s_i$. By \cite[\S (18.D) Corollary]{Matsumura} the Koszul complex $\text{Kos}_A(s_1,\ldots, s_i)$ defines a finite free resolution of $A/I$ as $A$-module. 
 
 Let $Y_0=Y\setminus Y\cap U$. By (4), there is a Zariski dense open subscheme $U_1$ of $G$ such that ${\mathcal O}_{gY}$ and ${\mathcal O}_Z$ are Tor-independent over ${\mathcal O}_H$ for all $g\in U_1(k)$; by (2) applied to $Y$ and $Y_0$, we may assume that $f^{-1}(g(Y\setminus Y_0))\cap Z^*$ contains each generic point of $f^{-1}(gY)\cap Z^*$. Thus, the Koszul complex $g\cdot \text{Kos}_A(s_1,\ldots, s_i)$ pulls back via $f$ to give a free resolution of ${\mathcal O}_{f^{-1}(gY)}$ on some affine open neighborhood $V$ of the generic points of $f^{-1}(gY)\cap Z^*$ in $Z$, hence $f^{-1}(gY)$ is defined by the regular sequence $f^*((g\cdot s_1)),\ldots, f^*(g\cdot s_i)$ on $V$ (here $g\in G(k)$ acts on the Koszul complex and the $s_i$ by $(g^{-1})^*(-)$).
 
 Taking $O(f, Y, Z^*, Z_0)$ to be the intersection of the open subsets satisfying (1)-(4) completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:TranslateRelation} Let $G$ be a $k$-rational algebraic group, and $H$ a $G$-homogeneous space. Let  $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair and    $f : X \to H$ a morphism. Let $G$ act on $H\times{\mathbb P}^1$ by the trivial
action on ${\mathbb P}^1$ (that is, $g . (y, u) = (gy, u)$). Let $W \subset H \times{\mathbb P}^1$ be a reduced closed subscheme of pure codimension $i$, flat over a neighborhood of $\{0,\infty\}$ in ${\mathbb P}^1$, and let $S\subset X$ be a closed subset of dimension $\le i-2$. For $g\in G(k)$, let
$W(g) := (f \times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1})^{-1}(gW ) \subset X\times{\mathbb P}^1$.
Then there exists a dense open subset $U(f, W, X^*, S) \subset G$ such that for all $g \in U(f,W, X^*,S)(k)$, the following
properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $W(g)$ is of pure  codimension $i$ in $X\times{\mathbb P}^1$.
\item $W(g)$ intersects $X^* \times{\mathbb P}^1$ and $X^* \times \{0,\infty\}$ properly, and
$W(g)\cap S\times{\mathbb P}^1=\0$.
\item $W(g)$ is a complete intersection in $X\times{\mathbb P}^1$ in a neighborhood of each generic point of
$W(g) \cap X^* \times{\mathbb P}^1$.
\item $W(g)$ is flat over a neighborhood of $\{0,\infty\}\subset{\mathbb P}^1$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, $U(f, W, X^*, S)(k)$ is Zariski dense in $U(f, W, X^*, S)$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The items (1)-(3) follow from  Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateCycle}, taking
\[
U(f, W, X^*, S)= O(f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1},W, X^*\times{\mathbb P}^1, S\times{\mathbb P}^1)\cap 
O(f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{\{0,\infty\}},W, X^*\times\{0,\infty\}, \0). 
\]
For (4), by generic flatness, $W(g)$ fails to be flat over ${\mathbb P}^1$ on a proper closed subset of ${\mathbb P}^1$, so we need only check flatness at $\{0,\infty\}$. This is a consequence of the  flatness of $W\subset H\times{\mathbb P}^1$ over a neighborhood of $\{0,\infty\}$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateCycle}(4) for the map $f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{\{0,\infty\}}$.

One could also reduce to   \cite[Lemma 6]{BS98},  by the same base-change argument we used to reduce the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateCycle} to \cite[Lemma 4]{BS98}.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:GenPosRelation} Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair and let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$. 
Let $Y\in {\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}^{\operatorname{\text{\rm qp}}}_k$ be smooth over $k$, and let $W\subset Y\times{\mathbb P}^1$ be a reduced closed subscheme of pure codimension $d$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism. Let $W_f:=(f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}})^{-1}(W)$. suppose that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $W_f$ is of pure codimension $d$ on $X\times{\mathbb P}^1$.
\item[(b)]  $W_f\subset (X_{\operatorname{C-M}}\amalg X(d-1)^0)\times{\mathbb P}^1$
\item[(c)] $W_f\cap X^* \times{\mathbb P}^1$ is a finite set 
\item[(d)] $(f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}})^{-1}(W_{\operatorname{nlci}})\cap X^* \times{\mathbb P}^1=\0$
\item[(e)]  $W_f\cap X \times \{0,\infty\}$  is a closed subscheme of $(X\setminus X^*)\times \{0,\infty\}$, finite over $k$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $W_f\subset X\times{\mathbb P}^1$ satisfies the conditions \eqref{eqn:Properties}(iii.) and Remark~\ref{rem:CodimNotDim}(i$'$, ii$'$). Moreover, the 0-cycle
\[
p_{1*}(|W_f|\cdot (X\times\{0\}-X\times\{\infty\})
\]
is in $R^d(X, X^*)$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
By Remark~\ref{rem:lci}, $W_{\operatorname{lci}}$ is dense in $W$.


Remark~\ref{rem:CodimNotDim}(i$'$) follows from (a), (b) and (c). \eqref{eqn:Properties}(iii.) is (e). 

For Remark~\ref{rem:CodimNotDim}(ii$'$) let $W_{f{\operatorname{C-M}}}=W_f\cap X_{\operatorname{C-M}}\times{\mathbb P}^1$.  It follows from (b) that $W_{f{\operatorname{C-M}}}$ is closed in $X\times{\mathbb P}^1$ and is supported in the Cohen-Macaulay locus of $X\times{\mathbb P}^1$. Take $x\in W_{f{\operatorname{C-M}}}\cap X^* \times{\mathbb P}^1$, and let ${\mathcal I}_{W_f,x}\subset {\mathcal O}_{X\times{\mathbb P}^1,x}$ be the ideal of $W_f$ in the local ring ${\mathcal O}_{X\times{\mathbb P}^1,x}$. By (d),  $y:=(f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}})(x)$ is in $W_{\operatorname{lci}}$, so $W$ is defined by a regular sequence of length $d$, $s_1,\ldots, s_d$,  in a Zariski open neighborhood  of $y$ in $Y\times{\mathbb P}^1$, giving the generators $f^*(s_1),\ldots, f^*(s_d)$ of ${\mathcal I}_{W_f,x}$. Since $W_f$ has pure codimension $d$ and ${\mathcal O}_{X\times{\mathbb P}^1,x}$ is Cohen-Macaulay of dimension $\ge d$, this implies that $f^*(s_1),\ldots, f^*(s_d)$ is a regular sequence in ${\mathcal O}_{X\times{\mathbb P}^1,x}$; this verifies Remark~\ref{rem:CodimNotDim}(ii$'$).

The fact that $p_{1*}(|W_f|\cdot (X\times\{0\}-X\times\{\infty\})$ is in $R^d(X, X^*)$ follows from Remark~\ref{rem:CodimNotDim} and Theorem~\ref{thm:Relations}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:Parametrize} Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair and  let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$. Let $G$ be a   $k$-rational  linear algebraic group over $k$, $H$ a quasi-projective homogeneous space for $G$, $Y\subset H$ a reduced closed subscheme of pure codimension $d$ and $f:X\to H$ a morphism. Then there is a dense open subscheme $B$ of $G\times G$, a dominant  morphism   $v:B\times G\to G\times G$, and a reduced closed subscheme $\Sigma\subset B\times G\times H\times {\mathbb P}^1$ such that \\[5pt]
i. The projections $p_{12}:\Sigma\to B\times G$   and $p_4:\Sigma\to {\mathbb P}^1$ are both flat, \\[2pt]
ii. For $(b, g)\in B\times G$, the scheme-theoretic fiber $\Sigma_{b,g}$ is reduced and of pure codimension $d$ in $(H\times{\mathbb P}^1)_{k(b,g)}$.\\[2pt]
iii. For $(b,g)\in (B\times G)$, write $ v(b,g))=(g_1, g_2)\in G\times_kG$. Then we have the identity of fibers 
\[
\Sigma_{b,g}\otimes_{{\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^1}}k(0)=g_1\cdot Y,\ \Sigma_{b,g}\otimes_{{\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^1}}k(\infty)=g_2\cdot Y.
\]
iv. Let $G$ act on $B\times G\times H\times {\mathbb P}^1$ by $g'\cdot (b,g, h,t)=(b,g'\cdot g, g'\cdot h, t)$. Then $\Sigma$ is stable under this $G$-action and $(g'\Sigma)_{b,g}=\Sigma_{b, g'g}$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
In case $k$ is algebraically closed, this is proven in the beginning of the proof of \cite[Lemma 7]{BS98}, except that $B$ is not shown to be an open subscheme of $G\times G$; this is because it is not assumed in {\it loc. cit.} that $G$ is $k$-rational. We give here a construction of $B$, following the ideas in the proof of \cite[Lemma 7]{BS98} and the construction in \cite[\S 5.2]{BKS}. 

Let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_k G$. Let $\bar{G}$ be a projective closure of $G$. By assumption, there is a dense open subscheme $U_1\subset G$ with $U_1$ isomorphic to a dense open subscheme of ${\mathbb A}^d\subset {\mathbb P}^d$, via an open immersion $j:U_1\to {\mathbb A}^d$.  We have the morphism
\[
\lambda:(U_1\times U_1\setminus \Delta_{U_1})\times{\mathbb P}^1\to {\mathbb P}^d
\]
sending $(g_1, g_2)\times{\mathbb P}^1$ to the line $\ell_{j(g_1), j(g_2)}\subset {\mathbb P}^d$ spanned by $j(g_1)\neq j(g_2)\in {\mathbb P}^d$; the restriction of $\lambda$ to $(g_1, g_2)\times{\mathbb P}^1$ is uniquely determined by  the identities
\[
\lambda((g_1, g_2), 0)=j(g_1),\ \lambda((g_1, g_2), \infty)=j(g_2),\ \lambda((g_1, g_2), 1)=\ell_{j(g_1), j(g_2)}\cap({\mathbb P}^d\setminus{\mathbb A}^d).
\]


Over $V:=\lambda^{-1}(j(U_1))$, we can lift $\lambda$ to a morphism
\[
\lambda_V:V\to U_1, j\circ\lambda_V=\lambda|_V.
\]
For $\eta$ the generic point of $U_1\times U_1$,   $\eta\times {\mathbb P}^1\cap V$ is a dense open subscheme of $\eta\times{\mathbb P}^1$, hence the restriction of  $\lambda_V$ to $\eta\times {\mathbb P}^1\cap V$ extends uniquely to a morphism $\lambda_\eta:\eta\times{\mathbb P}^1\to \bar{G}$. Thus, there is a dense open subscheme $B$ of $U_1\times U_1\setminus\Delta_{U_1}$ such that the restriction of $\lambda_V$ to $B\times{\mathbb P}^1\cap V$ extends to a morphism
\[
p:B\times{\mathbb P}^1\to \bar{G}.
\]

By construction, $p(B\times\{0,\infty\})\subset U_1\subset G$, with
\[
p((g_1, g_2)\times\{0\})=g_1,\ p((g_1, g_2)\times\{\infty\})=g_2
\]
for $(g_1, g_2)\in B\subset U_1\times U_1$. Moreover the projections $p_1, p_2:B\to U_1$ both have dense image and since $B\subset U_1\times U_1$ and $U_1$ is an open subset of an affine space, this implies that $p_1, p_2:B(k)\to U_1(k)$ both have dense image as well.

Let $\Sigma\subset B\times G\times H\times{\mathbb P}^1$ be the closure of 
\[
\Sigma^0:=\{(b, g, h, t)\in B\times G\times H\times{\mathbb P}^1\mid p(b,t)\in G, h\in g\cdot p(b,t)\cdot Y\}
\]
with projection $\pi:\Sigma\to G\times B\times {\mathbb P}^1$ mapping $(b, g, h, t)$ to $(g, b,t)$. We have the open subscheme $p^{-1}(G)\subset B\times{\mathbb P}^1$, giving the open subscheme 
$G\times p^{-1}(G)$ of $G\times B\times{\mathbb P}^1$, with
\[
\pi(\Sigma^0)=G\times p^{-1}(G)
\]
and with $\Sigma^0$ closed in $\pi^{-1}(G\times p^{-1}(G))$. Moreover, for $(b,t)\in p^{-1}(G)$, we have
\[
\pi^{-1}(g,b,t)=\{(b,g)\}\times g\cdot p(b,t)\cdot Y\times \{t\}\cong g\cdot p(b,t)\cdot Y,
\]
the isomorphism as schemes over $k(g,b,t)$. 

Let $\tau$ be the automorphism of $G\times G\times G$ with $\tau(g_1, g_2, g)=(g, g_1, g_2)$, and define the  morphism $v:B\times G\to G\times G$ as the composition
\[
B\times G\hookrightarrow (G\times G)\times G\xrightarrow{\tau}G\times (G\times G)\xrightarrow{(\mu\circ p_{12}, \mu\circ p_{13})}G\times G
\]
that is 
\[
v(b, g)=v((g_1, g_2), g)=(gg_1, gg_2).
\]


In case $G$ is a product of general linear groups, the open immersion $\operatorname{GL}_n\subset M_{n\times n}={\mathbb A}^{n^2}$ writes $G$ as an open subscheme of an affine space ${\mathbb A}^N$, so one can take $U_1=G$, $\bar{G}={\mathbb P}^N$; this is the setting used in \cite{BKS}. The arguments used to prove  \cite[\S 3.3, Lemmas 5.6, 5.7, 5.9]{BKS} carry over with minor changes to give a proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:Parametrize}; note that we may need to shrink $B$ so that (i)-(iv) all hold.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:TranslationPullback}
Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair and  let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$.  Let $H$ be a quasi-projective homogeneous space for a strongly $k$-rational linear algebraic group $G$, and let
$Y$ be a reduced closed subscheme  of $H$ of pure codimension $d$. Let  $f:X \to H$ be a morphism. There is a dense open subset $V(f, Y, X^*)$ of $G$  such that, for all $g_1, g_2\in V(f,Y, X^*)(k)$, we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item  The subschemes $f^{-1}(g_1Y)$, $f^{-1}(g_2)(Y)$ of $X$  are of pure codimension $d$, supported in $X\setminus X^*$. 
\item Letting $[f^{-1}(g_iY)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$ denote the class of the zero-cycle 
\[
|f^{-1}(g_iY)|\in Z^d(X\setminus X^*),\ i=1,2,
\] 
we have
\[
[f^{-1}(g_1Y)]=[f^{-1}(g_2Y)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*).
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Our proof closely follows the proof of \cite[Lemma 7]{BS98} and the discussion in \cite[\S 6.1, 6.2]{BKS}.

From Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateCycle} we have the dense open subset $O(f, Y, X^*,\0)$ of $G$ such that, for all $h_1, h_2\in O(f, Y, X^*,\0)(k)$, the closed subschemes  $f^{-1}(h_1Y)$ and $f^{-1}(h_2Y)$ of $X$  are of pure codimension $d$, supported in $X\setminus X^*$. Indeed,  by Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateCycle}(1), $f^{-1}(h_iY)$ has pure codimension $d$ for $i=1,2$. Since each component of $X^*$ has dimension $\le d-1$,  $f^{-1}(h_iY)\cap X^*=\0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateCycle}(2b).

For $(b,g)\in B\times G$, recall from Lemma~\ref{lem:Parametrize} that the fiber $\Sigma_{b,g}$ is a reduced closed subscheme of $(H\times{\mathbb P}^1)_{k(b,g)}$. Let $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{b,g}:=(f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}})^{-1}(\Sigma_{b,g})$. 


 Recall the dominant morphism $v:B\times G\to G\times G$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:Parametrize} and
let $T\subset v^{-1}(O(f, Y, X^*,\0)\times O(f, Y, X^*,\0))\subset B\times G$ be the subset consisting of points $(b,g)$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{b,g}$ is of pure codimension $d$ on $(X\times{\mathbb P}^1)_{k(b,g)}$.
\item[(b)]  $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{b,g}\subset (X_{\operatorname{C-M}}\amalg X(d-1)^0)\times{\mathbb P}^1_{k(b,g)}$
\item[(c)] $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{b,g}\cap X^* \times{\mathbb P}^1_{k(b,g)}$ is a finite set 
\item[(d)] $(f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}})^{-1}((\Sigma_{b,g})_{\operatorname{nlci}})\cap X^* \times{\mathbb P}^1_{k(b,g)}=\0$
\item[(e)]  $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{b,g}\cap X_{k(b,g)} \times \{0,\infty\}$  is a closed subscheme of $(X\setminus X^*)_{k(b,g)}\times \{0,\infty\}$, finite over $k(b,g)$.
\end{enumerate}
 

As noted in \cite[Lemma 6.1]{BKS} and in the  proof of \cite[Lemma 7]{BS98},   $T$ is a constructible subset of $B\times G$. Indeed, let 
\[
\tilde{\Sigma}=({\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{B\times G}\times f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1})^{-1}(\Sigma)\subset B\times G\times X\times{\mathbb P}^1. 
\]
Then conditions (a), (b), (c), (e) can be phrased as saying that the fiber of  
$\tilde{\Sigma}\cap B\times G\times F$ has dimension $\le r$ for suitable closed subsets $F$ of $X\times{\mathbb P}^1$ and integers $r$, a constructible condition. Condition (d) is similar, replacing $\Sigma$ with $\Sigma_{\operatorname{nlci}}$,  replacing $\tilde{\Sigma}$ with $({\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{B\times G}\times f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1})^{-1}(\Sigma_{\operatorname{nlci}})$ and taking $F=X^* \times{\mathbb P}^1$, $r=-1$. This shows that (d) defines a constructible condition, since   $(\Sigma_{b,g})_{\operatorname{nlci}}= (\Sigma_{\operatorname{nlci}})_{b,g}$ because $\Sigma\to B\times G$ is flat. 


By Theorem~\ref{thm:Relations} and Lemma~\ref{lem:GenPosRelation},   the 0-cycle
\[
p_{1*}(|\widetilde{\Sigma}_{b,g}|\cdot(X\times\{0\}-X\times\{\infty\})
\]
is a well-defined element of $R^d(X,X^*)$ for all $(b,g)\in T(k)$. Moreover,  if $v(b,g)=(g_1, g_2)$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eqn:ParamRelation}
|f^{-1}(g_1Y)|-|f^{-1}(g_2Y)|=p_{1*}(|\widetilde{\Sigma}_{b,g}|\cdot (X\times\{0\}-X\times\{\infty\})
\end{equation}
hence $|f^{-1}(g_1Y)|-|f^{-1}(g_2Y)|$ is in $R^d(X, X^*)$.  


We claim that $T$ contains an open dense subset $U$ of $B\times G$. To see this,  let $S=X\setminus  (X_{\operatorname{C-M}}\amalg X(d-1)^0)$; following Remark~\ref{rem:Prelims}, we see that ${\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kS\le d-2$. Now take an arbitrary $(b,g)\in B(k)\times G(k)$, giving $\Sigma_{b,g}\subset H\times {\mathbb P}^1$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateRelation}, we have the open subset $U(f, \Sigma_{b,g}, X^*, S)$ of $G$ such that for all $g'\in U(f, \Sigma_{b,g}, X^*, S)$, $(f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}})^{-1}(g'\Sigma_{b,g})$ satisfies the conditions (a)-(e) above. But since $g'\Sigma_{b,g}=\Sigma_{b, g'g}$, it follows that $T\cap b\times G$ contains the open subscheme $b\times U(f, \Sigma_{b,g}, X^*,S)\cdot g$, and since $T$ is constructible and $B(k)$ is Zariski dense in $B$, it follows that $T$ must contain a dense open subset $U$ of $B\times G$.


Since $v:B\times G\to G\times G$ is an open morphism, we have the dense open subset $v(U)\subset G\times G$. Fix a $g_0\in G(k)$ such that $g_0\times G\cap v(U)$ is open in $g_0\times G$ and let 
\[
V(f, Y, X^*)=p_2(g_0\times G\cap v(U)). 
\]
Note that the map $v:U(k)\to v(U)(k)$ is surjective, since $G$ is strongly $k$-rational. For $g_1, g_2\in V(f,Y, X^*)(k)$, choose $(b_i, h_i)\in U(k)$ with $v(b_i, h_i)=(g_0, g_i)$, $i=1,2$. Then by \eqref{eqn:ParamRelation}, the cycles
\[
|f^{-1}(g_0Y)|, |f^{-1}(g_1Y)|, |f^{-1}(g_2Y)|
\]
are all well-defined 0-cycles in $Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$ and
\[
[f^{-1}(g_iY)]=[f^{-1}(g_0Y)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*),\ i=1,2,
\]
hence $[f^{-1}(g_1Y)]=[f^{-1}(g_2Y)]$, which completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:HomogFunct} Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair and  let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$.   Let $H$ be a quasi-projective homogeneous space for a strongly $k$-rational linear algebraic group $G$, and let $f:X\to H$ be a morphism. There is a group homomorphism $f^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$ such that,  given $z\in Z^d(H)$ with class $[z]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)$, there a dense open subset $U_{f,z}$ of $G$ such that for all $g\in U_{f,z}(k)$,   we have
\begin{enumerate}\label{thm:1}
\item[(a)] $f^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(g\cdot z))\subset X\setminus X^*$,
\item[(b)] $f^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(g\cdot z))$ has pure codimension $d$ on $X$ and the cycle-theoretic pull-back $f^*(g\cdot z)\in Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$ is defined. 
\item[(c)] $[f^*(g\cdot z)]=f^*([z])\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X,X^*)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Write $z=\sum_{i=1}^nm_iY_i$ with the $Y_i$ codimension $d$ integral closed subschemes of $H$. We have the dense open subsets $V(f, Y_i, X^*)\subset G$ given by Proposition~\ref{prop:TranslationPullback}. Let $U_{f,z}=\cap_{i=1}^nV(f, Y_i, X^*)$, and choose $g\in U_{f,z}(k)$. Then (a), (b) for $g\cdot z$ follow from Proposition~\ref{prop:TranslationPullback}, giving us the well-defined cycle $f^*(g\cdot z)\in Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$. Moreover, for each $i$, the class $[f^*(g\cdot Y_i)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$ is independent of the choice of $g\in U_{f,z}(k)$, hence the same follows for the class $[f^*(g\cdot z)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$. Thus, sending $z\in Z^d(H)$ to $[f^*(g\cdot z)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$ for some $g\in U(f,z)(k)$ gives  a well-defined group homomorphism
\[
\tilde{f}^*:Z^d(H)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*).
\]

Now suppose we have a second codimension $d$ cycle $z'=\sum_{i=1}^{n'}m'_iY'_i$, and take $g'\in U_{f,z'}$, giving the well-defined  cycle $f^*(g'\cdot z')\in Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$, with class $[f^*(g'\cdot z')]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$ independent of the choice of $g'$. Supposing that $[z]=[z']\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)$, we claim that 
\begin{equation}\label{eqn:RationalEquivPullback}
[f^*(g\cdot z)] = [f^*(g'\cdot z')]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*),
\end{equation}
which will show that $\tilde{f}^*$ descends to a well-defined group homomorphism
\[
f^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*),
\]
proving (c). 

Since $G$ is $k$-rational, the action of $G(k)$ on $H$ induces the trivial action on ${\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)$, so $[z]=[z']\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)$ implies that $[h\cdot z]= [h'\cdot z']$ for all $h, h'\in G(k)$. To verify \eqref{eqn:RationalEquivPullback}, choose a codimension $d$ cycle $W\subset H\times{\mathbb P}^1$ with
\[
g\cdot z-g'z'=p_{1*}(W\cdot (H\times\{0\}-H\times\{\infty\})).
\]
It follows easily from Lemmas~\ref{lem:TranslateRelation}, \ref{lem:GenPosRelation} that there is a dense open subset $U(f, W, X^*)\subset G$ such that, for all $g''\in U(f, W, X^*)(k)$, the pullback cycle $((g''\cdot f)\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1})^*(W)$ is a well-defined codimension $d$ cycle on $X\times{\mathbb P}^1$, the intersection products
\[
p_{1*}((f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1})^*((g''\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}})\cdot W)\cdot (X\times\{0\})),\ 
p_{1*}((f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1})^*((g''\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}})\cdot W)\cdot (X\times\{\infty\}))
\]
are well defined and supported in $X\setminus X^*$, and the cycle
\[
p_{1*}((f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1})^*((g''\times {\operatorname{\rm Id}})W)\cdot (X\times\{0\}-X\times\{\infty\}))
\]
is in $R^d(X, X^*)$. We may take $g''\in U(f, W, X^*)(k)$ such that $g''g\in U_{f, z}(k)$ and $g''g'\in U_{f, z'}(k)$, so
\[
p_{1*}((f\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^1})^*((g''\times {\operatorname{\rm Id}})W)\cdot (X\times\{0\}-X\times\{\infty\})) = f^*(g''gz)-f^*(g''g'z')
\] 
and thus
\[
[f^*(gz)]=[f^*(g''gz)]=[f^*(g''g'z')]=[f^*(g'z')]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*),
\]
completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
\label{rem:SmoothCase}Theorem~\ref{thm:HomogFunct} is a partial generalization of a classical result in intersection theory.

Let $f:Y\to Z$ be a morphism of a smooth $k$-schemes. We have the well-defined group homomorphism
\[
f^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(Z)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y).
\]
Moreover, if $z\in Z^d(Z)$ is a codimension $d$ cycle such that $f^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(z))$ is a pure codimension $d$ closed subset of $Y$, then the cycle-theoretic pullback $f^*(z)\in Z^d(Y)$ is defined and $f^*([z])=[f^*(z)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y)$ (see \cite[\S 20.4]{Fulton}).

If we now take $Z=H$, a homogeneous space for a $k$-rational linear algebraic group $G$, then $G(k)$ acts trivially on ${\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)$, that is $[z]=[g\cdot z]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)$ for $z\in Z^d(H)$, $g\in G(k)$
Moreover, by Kleiman's transversality theorem \cite[Theorem 2]{Kleiman}, there is a dense open subset $U_{f, z}\subset G$ such that for $g\in U_{f, z}(k)$, $f^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(gz))$ has pure codimension $d$ on $Y$, so $f^*(g\cdot z)$ is a well-defined codimension $d$ cycle on $Y$. Thus,  by the above discussion, we have
\[
f^*([z])=f^*([g\cdot z])=[f^*(g\cdot z)].
\]
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:HomogFunctoriality} Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair and  let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$. Suppose we have a homomorphism of strongly $k$-rational linear algebraic groups $\rho:G_1\to G_2$, quasi-projective homogeneous spaces $H_i$ for $G_i$, $i=1,2$, a morphism $p:H_1\to H_2$ that is  $G_1$-equivariant via $\rho$, and finally, a morphism $f:X\to H_1$. Then the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H_2)\ar[rr]^{p^*}\ar[dr]_{(pf)^*}&&{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H_1)\ar[dl]^{f^*}\\
&{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)
}
\]
commutes.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Take a codimension $d$ cycle $z\in Z^d(H_2)$. Applying Remark~\ref{rem:SmoothCase} to the morphisms $p$, we have the dense open subset $U_{p,z}\subset G_2$ such that for all $g_2\in  U_{p,z}(k)$ $p^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(g\cdot z))$ has pure codimension $d$ on $H_1$, giving the well-defined codimension $d$ cycle $p^*(g_2\cdot z)$ on $H_1$, and we have
\[
p^*[z]=[p^*(g_2\cdot z)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(H_1).
\]


Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:HomogFunct} to the morphism $f$, we see that for each $g_1\in U_{f, p^*(g_2\cdot z)}(k)$, the cycle $f^*(g_1\cdot p^*(g_2\cdot z))$ is a well-defined 0-cycle on $X$, supported in $X\setminus X^*$, and 
\[
[f^*(g_1\cdot p^*(g_2\cdot z))]=f^*([p^*(g_2\cdot z))]).
\]
We may assume that $\rho(g_1)g_2$ is in $U_{pf, z}(k)\cap U_{p,z}(k)$, so $(pf)^*(\rho(g_1)g_2\cdot z)$ is a well-defined 0-cycle on $X$, supported in $X\setminus X^*$,  with
\[
(pf)^*([z])=[(pf)^*(\rho(g_1)g_2\cdot z)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*),
\]
and $p^*(\rho(g_1)g_2\cdot z)$ is a well-defined codimension $d$ cycle on $H_1$, with
\[
p^*[z]=[p^*(\rho(g_1)g_2\cdot z)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(H_1).
\]

We have the identity of 0-cycles on $X\setminus X^*$
\[
(pf)^*(\rho(g_1)g_2\cdot z)=f^*(p^*(\rho(g_1)g_2\cdot z))=f^*(g_1\cdot p^*(g_2\cdot z)),
\]
which gives the identity of classes in ${\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$
\begin{align*}
(pf)^*([z])&=[(pf)^*(\rho(g_1)g_2\cdot z)]\\
&=[f^*(p^*(\rho(g_1)g_2\cdot z))]\\
&=[f^*(g_1\cdot p^*(g_2\cdot z))]\\
&=f^*([p^*(g_2\cdot z)])\\
&=f^*(p^*([z])).
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:PullbackFunct3} Let $(X, X^*)$, $(Y, Y^*)$ be admissible pairs with   ${\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kY$, and let $q:Y\to X$ be a morphism; we suppose  the conditions (i)-(iii) of Lemma~\ref{lem:EtalePullback} are satisfied for $q$, giving the pullback map 
\[
q^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*),\ d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX.
\]
Let $f:X\to H$ be a morphism to a homogeneous space $H$ for a strongly $k$-rational linear algebraic group $G$,  as in Theorem~\ref{thm:HomogFunct}. Then all the morphisms in the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
&{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)\ar[dl]_{f^*}\ar[dr]^{(fq)^*}\\
{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)
\ar[rr]^{q^*}&&{\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)\ 
}
\]
are  defined, and the diagram commutes.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Note that $(fq)^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)$, $f^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$ are defined following Theorem~\ref{thm:HomogFunct}, and $q^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)$ is defined following Lemma~\ref{lem:EtalePullback}. For $z\in Z^d(H)$, take $g\in U_{z,f}(k)\cap U_{z,fq}(k)$, so the cycle pullbacks $f^*(g\cdot z)\in Z^d(X\setminus X^*)$ and $(fq)^*(g\cdot z)\in Z^d(Y\setminus Y^*)$ are defined and
\[
f^*([z])=[f^*(g\cdot z)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*),\ (fq)^*([z])=[(fq)^*(g\cdot z)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*).
\]
Moreover $f^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(g\cdot z))$ has pure codimension $d$ on $X$ and $(fq)^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(g\cdot z))$ has pure codimension $d$ on $Y$. Thus $q^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(f^*(g\cdot z))\subset (fq)^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(g\cdot z))$ also has pure codimension $d$ on $Y$, so $q^*(f^*(g\cdot z))$ is defined and 
$q^*(f^*(g\cdot z))=(fq)^*(g\cdot z)\in Z^d(Y\setminus Y^*)$. 
Since $q^*([f^*([z])])=[q^*(f^*(g\cdot z))]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)$, we thus have
\[
q^*([f^*([z])])=(fq)^*([z])
\]
in ${\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)$, as claimed.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:BCCompat} Let $k\hookrightarrow F$ be an extension of fields, let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair over $k$, and let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$. We suppose the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:base-change} are satisfied, giving the pullback map $p_X^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X_F, X_F^*)$.\\[5pt]
1. Let $f:X\to H$ be a morphism to a homogeneous space $H$ for a strongly $k$-rational linear algebraic group $G$, giving the base-change $f_F:X_F\to H_F:=H\times_kF$. Then $G_F:G\times_kF$ is a strongly $F$-rational linear algebraic group over $F$ and  $H_F$ is a homogeneous space for $G_F$. Moreover, letting $p_H:H_F\to H$, $p_X:X_F\to X$ be the projections, the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)\ar[r]^{f^*}\ar[d]^{p_H^*}&{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\ar[d]^{p_X^*}\\
{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H_F)\ar[r]^{f_F^*}&{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X_F, X_F^*)
}
\]
commutes.   \\[2pt]
2. Let  $(Y, Y^*)$ be an admissible pair over $k$ with ${\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kY={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$ and let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism satisfying the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:EtalePullback}, giving the pullback map $f^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)$. Suppose that $(X_F, X_F^*)$ and  $(Y_F, Y_F^*)$ satisfy the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:base-change}, giving the pullback maps $p_X^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X_F, X_F^*)$, $p_Y^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y_F, Y_F^*)$. Then  $f_F:Y_F\to X_F$ satisfies the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:EtalePullback}, and the diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)\ar[r]^{f^*}\ar[d]^{p_X^*}&{\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y, Y^*)\ar[d]^{p_Y^*}\\
{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X_F, X_F^*)\ar[r]^{f_F^*}&{\operatorname{CH}}^d(Y_F, Y_F^*)
}
\]
commutes, where the vertical maps are the base-change maps of Lemma~\ref{lem:base-change}.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
For (1), if we have a cycle $z\in Z^d(H)$ such that $f^{-1}({\rm supp}\, z)$ has codimension $d$ on $X$ and is contained in $X_{\operatorname{reg}}$, then the base-change $p_H^*(z)$ is in $Z^d(H_F)$ and $f_F^{-1}({\rm supp}\,(p_H^*(z)))$ also has codimension $d$ on $X_F$. Thus the pull-backs $f^*(z)$, $f_F^*(p_H^*(z))$ are defined. Moreover, the restriction of $f$ to  $f:X_{\operatorname{reg}}\to H$ is an lci-morphism, since a locally closed immersion $X_{\operatorname{reg}}\hookrightarrow {\mathbb P}^N_k$ is a regular embedding, by \cite[Proposition 19.1.1]{EGAIV4}.  Thus $f_F:(X_{\operatorname{reg}})_F\to H_F$ is also an lci morphism and 
 \[
p_X^*(f^*(z))=f_F^*(p_H^*(z))
\]
as cycles on $X_F$, using  \cite[Theorem 6.2, Theorem 6.6]{Fulton} and the fact that lci pullback is induced by the cycle-theoretic pullback when the latter is defined \cite[\S 7.1, \S 20.4]{Fulton}.

On the other hand, given an arbitrary  $y=\sum_in_iY_i\in Z^d(H)$ with the $Y_i$ integral, there is a dense open subset $U$ of $U_{f,y}:=\cap_iV(f,Y_i,X^*)$ such that for $g\in U(k)$, if we consider $g$ as in $G(F)=G_F(F)$ via the map ${\rm Spec\,} F\to {\rm Spec\,} k$ induced by $k\subset F$, $g$ is in $U_{f_F, p_H^*(y)}:=\cap_iV(f_F,(Y_i\times_kF)_{\rm red},X^*)$. Thus $f^*([y])=[f^*(g\cdot y)]$, $f_F^*([p_H^*(y)])=[f_F^*(g\cdot p_H^*(y))]$,  and hence
\begin{multline*}
f_F^*(p_H^*([y]))=f_F^*([p_H^*(y)])=[f_F^*(g\cdot p_H^*(y))]=[f_F^*( p_H^*(g\cdot y))]\\
=[p_X^*(f^*(g\cdot y))]=p_X^*([f^*(g\cdot y)])=p_X^*(f^*([y])).
\end{multline*}

For (2), it is an easy consequence of well-known properties of flat base-change that $f_F:Y_F\to X_F$ satisfies the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:EtalePullback} since $f:Y\to X$ does.  Then (2) follows by the functoriality of cycle pullback for compositions of flat morphisms.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:RatEquivPullback}
Let $(X, X^*)$ be an admissible pair and  let $d={\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kX$. Let $H$ be a quasi-projective homogeneous space for a strongly $k$-rational linear algebraic group $G$,  let $f:X\times{\mathbb P}^1\to H$ be a morphism and let $W\subset H$ be a reduced closed subscheme of pure codimension $d$. Then there is a dense open subset $U^*_{f,W, X^*}$ of $G$ such that, for all $g\in U^*_{f,W, X^*}(k)$, we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f^{-1}(g\cdot W)$ is a  closed subscheme of $X\times{\mathbb P}^1$ of pure codimension $d$,   supported in $(X_{\operatorname{C-M}}\amalg X(d-1)^0)\times{\mathbb P}^1$.
\item $f^{-1}(g\cdot W)\cap (X\times\{0,\infty\})$ is a closed subscheme  of pure codimension $d$, supported in $(X\setminus X^*)\times\{0,\infty\}$.
\item $f^{-1}(g\cdot W)\cap (X^*\times{\mathbb P}^1)$ is a finite set, and $f^{-1}(g\cdot W)$ is defined by a regular sequence (of length $d$) in a neighborhood of $f^{-1}(W)\cap X^*\times{\mathbb P}^1$.
\item Let $|gW|\in Z^d(H)$ denote the cycle associated to the closed subscheme $gW$, and let $f_0, f_\infty:X\to H$ be the restriction of $f$ to $X\times\{0\}$, $X\times\{\infty\}$, respectively. The cycle-theoretic pull-backs $f^*(|gW|)$, $f_0^*(|gW|)$ and $f_\infty^*(|gW|)$ are all defined, and 
$f_0^*(|gW|)$ and $f_\infty^*(|gW|)$ are supported in $X\setminus X^*$.
\item For $i=0,\infty$,  the cycle class $[f^*_i(|gW|)]\in {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$ satisfies
\[
[f^*_i(|g\cdot W|)]=f_i^*([W])\in{\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*),
\]
where $f_i^*:{\operatorname{CH}}^d(H)\to {\operatorname{CH}}^d(X, X^*)$ is the pullback map of Theorem~\ref{thm:HomogFunct}
\item $p_{1*}(|f^{-1}(gW)|\cdot(X\times\{0\}-X\times\{\infty\})=f_0^*(|gW|)-f_\infty^*(|gW|)$, and this 0-cycle 
is in $R^d(X, X^*)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Let $S:= X\setminus (X_{\operatorname{C-M}}\amalg X(d-1)^0)$ and let 
\[
U^*_{f,W, X^*}=U(f,W, X^*, S)\cap   U_{f_0,|W|}\cap U_{f_\infty, |W|}. 
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateCycle}, $U^*_{f,W, X^*}$ is a dense open subset of $G$ and $U^*_{f,W, X^*}(k)$ is dense in $U^*_{f,W, X^*}$. 

 (4) and (6) follow from (1)-(3), using Remark~\ref{rem:CodimNotDim}. Similarly, since $U^*_{f, W, X^*}\subset  U_{f_0,|W|}\cap U_{f_\infty, |W|}$, (5) follows from the definition of the pullback maps $f_0^*$, $f_\infty^*$ given in  Theorem~\ref{thm:HomogFunct}. 

For $g\in U(f,W, X^*, S)(k)$, the properties (1)  and (3) are satisfied by Lemma~\ref{lem:TranslateRelation} and similarly, property (2) is satisfied  for $g\in (U_{f_0,|W|}\cap U_{f_\infty, |W|})(k)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:HomogFunct}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{def:EquivRel1} We let $\sim_{m,M}$ denote the equivalence relation on the presheaf 
\[
{\rm Hom}_k(-, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M)):{\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}_k^{\text{\rm op}}\to {\mathbf{Sets}}
\]
generated by  the two relations:
\\[5pt]
1. $\phi\sim_{m,M}  g\cdot \phi$ for $\phi\in {\rm Hom}_k(Z, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M))$, $g\in \operatorname{GL}_M(k)$\\[2pt]
2. Given $M'<M$,  $\phi':Z\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M')$ represented by $(E, f_1,\ldots, f_{M'})$,  and $M-M'$ generating sections $f_{M'+1},\ldots, f_M$ of $E$, let $\phi:Z\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M)$ be the morphism given by $(E, f_1,\ldots, f_M)$. Then $\phi\sim_{m,M} i_{m, M,M'}\circ \phi'$.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:GloballyGen}  Sending $f:Z\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M)$ to the class of $f^*E_{m,M}$ in ${\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m^{\operatorname{gl}}(Z)$ induces a bijection
\[
\Phi^{\operatorname{gl}}(Z):{\mathop{\rm colim}}_M{\rm Hom}(Z, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M))/\sim_{m,M}\to {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m^{\operatorname{gl}}(Z)
\]
natural in $Z$. Here the maps in the colimit are induced by the closed immersions $i_{M_2,M_1}$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
We first check that $i_{m,M_2, M_1 *}:{\rm Hom}(-, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_1))\to {\rm Hom}(-, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_2))$ descends to a map ${\rm Hom}(-, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_1))/\sim_{m, M_1}\to {\rm Hom}(-, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M_2))/\sim_{m, M_2}$. The relation (1) of Definition~\ref{def:EquivRel1} is respected since $i_{m,M_2, M_1}$ is $\rho_{M_2, M_1}$-equivariant. Suppose we are given $M'_1<M_1$, a rank $m$ locally free sheaf $E$ with generating sections  $f_1,\ldots, f_{M_1'}$, and $f_{M_1'+1},\ldots, f_{M_1}$ as in Definition~\ref{def:EquivRel1}(2),  giving morphisms $\phi':Z\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_1')$ representing $(E, 
f_1,\ldots, f_{M_1'})$ and $\phi:Z\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_1)$ representing $(E, 
f_1,\ldots, f_{M_1})$. We then have $\phi\sim i_{m, M_1,M_1'}\phi'$, and we need to show that $i_{m, M_2,M_1}\phi\sim_{m, M_2} i_{m, M_2, M_1}(i_{m, M_1, M_1'}\phi')$. 

We have $i_{m, M_2, M_1}\circ i_{m, M_1, M_1'}=i_{m, M_2, M_1'}$, 
$i_{m, M_2,M_1}\phi$ is the morphism representing $(E, f_1,\ldots, f_{M_1}, 0_{M_1+1},\ldots, 0_{M_2})$ and $i_{m, M_2, M_1'}\phi'$ is the morphism representing 
$(E, f_1,\ldots, f_{M_1'}, 0_{M_1'+1},\ldots, 0_{M_2})$. Using the relation $\sim_{m, M_2}$ for the generating sections $f_1,\ldots, f_{M_1'}$ and $(f_{M_1'+1},\ldots, f_{M_1},  0_{M_1+1},\ldots, 0_{M_2})$ gives
\[
i_{m, M_2,M_1}\phi\sim_{m, M_2} i_{m, M_2, M_1'}\phi'= i_{m, M_2, M_1}(i_{m, M_1, M_1'}\phi')
\]
as desired.


Since the relation $\sim_{m,M}$ and the maps $i_{m, M_2,M_1}$ only change the choice of 
generating sections, and not the isomorphism class of the locally free sheaf, the map $(f:Z\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M))\mapsto f^*E_{m, M}$ descends to a well-defined natural transformation 
\[
\Phi^{\operatorname{gl}}:{\mathop{\rm colim}}_M{\rm Hom}(-, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M))/\sim_{m,M}\to {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m^{\operatorname{gl}}. 
\]
As every  rank $m$ vector bundle $E$ generated by $M$ sections is isomorphic to $f^*E_{m,M}$ for suitable $f:Z\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M)$, we see that $\Phi^{\operatorname{gl}}$ is surjective.

Now, given a globally generated rank $m$ $E$ on $Z$, and two sets of global generators $(f_1,\ldots , f_M)$, $(f_1',\ldots , f'_{M'})$ with corresponding morphisms $\phi$, $\phi'$, we have the global generators $(f_1,\ldots , f_{M+M'})$, with $f_{M+i}=f'_i$ for $i=1,\ldots, M'$, with corresponding morphism $\phi''$, and  
\[
i_{m, M+M',M}\circ \phi\sim_{m, M+M'}
\phi''\sim_{m, M+M'}i_{m, M+M',M'}\circ\phi'.
\]
Thus,  $\phi$ and $\phi'$ map to the same element in  
${\mathop{\rm colim}}_M{\rm Hom}(Z, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M))/\sim_{m,M}$, and hence $\Phi^{\operatorname{gl}}$ is injective.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:TensorIdentity} We have\\[5pt]
1. $\lambda_{N, N', m,M}^*(E_{m, M''}(-1))\cong E_{m, M}(0,1)(-1,-1)\cong E_{m, M}(-1,0)=p_{13}^*(E_{m, M}(-1))$.\\[2pt]
2. Give ${\mathbb P}^N$, ${\mathbb P}^{N'}$, ${\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M)$ and ${\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M'')$ the usual actions of $\operatorname{GL}_{N+1}$,  $\operatorname{GL}_{N'+1}$, $\operatorname{GL}_M$ and $\operatorname{GL}_{M''}$.  Let $\rho:=\rho_{N,N'}:\operatorname{GL}_{N+1}\times \operatorname{GL}_{N'+1}\to \operatorname{GL}_{N''+1}$ be the tensor product representation, corresponding to the isomorphism induced by $\psi_{N, N'}$
\[
H^0({\mathbb P}^N, {\mathcal O}(1))\otimes_kH^0({\mathbb P}^{N'}, {\mathcal O}(1))\cong H^0({\mathbb P}^{N''}, {\mathcal O}(1))
\]
and let $\tau:=\tau_{N', m, M}: \operatorname{GL}_{N'+1}\times \operatorname{GL}_M\to \operatorname{GL}_{M''}$ be the representation induced by the canonical isomorphism
\begin{align*}
H^0({\mathbb P}^{N'}, {\mathcal O}(1))\otimes_k H^0({\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M), E_{m, M})&\cong H^0({\mathbb P}^{N'}\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M), E_{m, M}(1))\\&\cong H^0({\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M''), E_{m, M''})
\end{align*}
given by $\phi_{N', m, M}$. Then $\lambda_{N, N', m,M}$ is equivariant with respect to the homomorphism
\[
\operatorname{GL}_{N+1}\times \operatorname{GL}_{N'+1}\times \operatorname{GL}_M\to \operatorname{GL}_{N''+1}\times \operatorname{GL}_{M''}
\]
sending $(g_1, g_2, g_3)$ to $(\rho(g_1, g_2), \tau(g_2, g_3))$.\\[2pt]
3. Identify ${\mathbb P}^N$ with ${\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(1, N+1)$, and write $i_{N', N}:{\mathbb P}^N\to {\mathbb P}^{N'}$ for $i_{1, N'+1, N+1}:{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(1, N+1)\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(1, N'+1)$.

For $N_1\le N_2$, $N_1'\le N_2'$,  $M_1\le M_2$, we have $N_1''\le N_2''$,  $M_1''\le M_2''$ and the diagram
\[
\xymatrixcolsep{70pt}
\xymatrix{
{\mathbb P}^{N_1}\times{\mathbb P}^{N_1'}\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_1)\ar[d]^{i_{N_2, N_1}\times i_{N_2', N_1'}\times i_{m, M_2, M_1}}\ar[r]^{\lambda_{N_1, N_1', m, M_1}}&
{\mathbb P}^{N_1''}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_1'')\ar[d]^{i_{N_2'', N_1''}\times i_{m, M_2'', M_1''}}\\
{\mathbb P}^{N_2}\times{\mathbb P}^{N_2'}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_2)\ar[r]^{\lambda_{N_2, N_2', m, M_2}}
&{\mathbb P}^{N_2''}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_2'')
}
\]
commutes, up to the action of some $g\in\operatorname{GL}_{N_2''+1}(k)\times \operatorname{GL}_{M_2''}(k)$ on ${\mathbb P}^{N_2''}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M_2'')$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
For  (1), we have
\begin{align*}
\lambda_{N, N', m,M}^*(E_{m, M''}(-1))&=
(p_{12}^*\operatorname{Ver}_{N, N'}^*{\mathcal O}(-1)\otimes  p_{23}^*\phi_{N', m, M}^*E_{m, M''})\\
&=p_{23}^*E_{m, M}\otimes {\mathcal O}(0,1)\otimes {\mathcal O}(-1,-1)\\
&=E_{m, M}(-1,0).
\end{align*}
(2) and (3) are easy computations.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- not-1: body_md -->
Identifying ${\mathbb P}^N$ with ${\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(1, N+1)$, we write $\sim_N$ for the equivalence relation $\sim_{1, N+1}$ on ${\rm Hom}(-, {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(1, N+1))$. We let $\sim_{N, m, M}$ be the equivalence relation $\sim_{N}\times \sim_{m, M}$ on ${\rm Hom}(-, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M))$, and write $\overline{{\rm Hom}}(-, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))$ for ${{\rm Hom}}(-, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))/\sim_{N, m, M}$.
<!-- end not-1 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
The maps $p_{13}:{\mathbb P}^N\times{\mathbb P}^{N'}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M)\to {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M)$ and $\lambda_{N, N', m, M}: {\mathbb P}^N\times{\mathbb P}^{N'}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M)\to {\mathbb P}^{N''}\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M'')$ induce maps of presheaves on ${\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}_k$
\begin{multline*}
{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+}\widetilde{{\rm Hom}}(-, {\mathbb P}^{?_1}\times{\mathbb P}^{?_2}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, ?_3))\\
\xymatrix{\ar@<5pt>[r]^{p_{13}(-)}\ar@<-5pt>[r]_{\lambda(-,m)}&}
{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+}\overline{{\rm Hom}}(-, {\mathbb P}^{?_1}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, ?_2)).
\end{multline*}
Here the map $p_{13}(-)$ uses the map $p_{13}:{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+\to {\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+$ and the map $\lambda(-,m)$ uses the map $(N, N', M)\mapsto (N'', M'')$ on the index posets to define the maps on the colimits.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
The fact that $p_{13}(-)$ and $\lambda(-,m)$ are well-defined follows directly from Lemma~\ref{lem:TensorIdentity}.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:VectmPresentation} Let $X$ be a quasi-projective $k$-scheme. Sending $f:X\to {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M)$ to $f^*E_{m, M}(-1)\in {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)$ defines a bijection $\Psi(X, m)$:
\begin{align*}
{\operatorname{coeq}}[{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+}&\widetilde{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^{?_1}\times{\mathbb P}^{?_2}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, ?_3))\\&\xymatrix{\ar@<5pt>[r]^{p_{13}(X)}\ar@<-5pt>[r]_{\lambda(X,m)}&}
{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+}\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^{?_1}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, ?_2))]\xymatrix{\ar[r]^{\Psi(X, m)}_\sim&} {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X),
\end{align*}
natural in $X\in {\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}^{\operatorname{\text{\rm qp}}}_k$.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Let ${\rm Pic}^+(X)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of globally generated invertible sheaves on $X$, that is, ${\rm Pic}^+(X)={\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_1^{\operatorname{gl}}(X)$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:GloballyGen} that sending $f:X\to {\mathbb P}^N$ to $f^*{\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^N}(1)$ induces a bijection
\begin{equation}\label{eqn:PicDescr}
{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\mathbb N}_+}\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N)\xrightarrow{\sim} {\rm Pic}^+(X).
\end{equation}
Fixing one $L\in {\rm Pic}^+(X)$, let $\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N)_L$ be the subset of $\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N)$ consisting of the equivalence classes of morphisms $f:X\to {\mathbb P}^N$ such that $f^*{\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^N}(1)\cong L$. Similarly, let ${\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m^L(X)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of rank $m$ locally free sheaves $E$ such that $E\otimes L$ is globally generated and let $\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))_L$ be the subset of $\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))$ consisting of equivalence classes of maps $f:X\to {\mathbb P}^N\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M)$ such that $p_1\circ f$ is in 
$\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N)_L$. Then it is easy to see that for each $f\in \overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))_L$, $(p_2\circ f)^*(E_{m, M})$ is isomorphic to a sheaf of the form $E\otimes L$, with $E\in {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m^L(X)$, and   $f^*(E_{m, M}(-1))\cong E$. Thus, we have the well-defined map
\[
\phi_{N, m, M}^L:\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))_L\to {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m^L(X).
\]

Arguing as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:GloballyGen}, we see that the maps $\phi_{N, m, M}^L$ induce a bijection
\[
\phi^L:{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+}\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))_L\to {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m^L(X).
\]
If we now consider the entire colimit, we have the map
\[
\phi:{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+}\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))\to {\rm Pic}^+(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X).
\]
sending $f:X\to {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M)$ to the pair of classes $((p_1\circ f)^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^N}(1)), f^*(E_{m, M}(-1)))$. From our description of $\phi_L$, we see that $\phi$ is injective, with image of $\phi$ contained the subset 
\[
[{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+=\{(L, E)\mid E\otimes L\text{ is globally generated}\}\subset 
{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X).
\]
From \eqref{eqn:PicDescr}, it follows that 
\[
\phi:{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\mathbb N}_+\times{\mathbb N}_+}\overline{{\rm Hom}}(X, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))\to [{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+
\]
is a bijection.

Let $\le^*$ be partial order on ${\rm Pic}^+(X)$ defined by $L\le^* L\otimes L'$ for $L, L'\in {\rm Pic}^+(X)$. Note that $({\rm Pic}^+(X), \le^*)$ is right filtering since
\[
L\le^* L\otimes L',\ L'\le^* L'\otimes L=L\otimes L'
\]
for $L, L'\in {\rm Pic}^+(X)$. 
Given $L'\in {\rm Pic}^+(X)$, we have the map
\[
-\otimes L':[{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+\to [{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+
\]
sending $(L, E)$ to $(L\otimes L', E)$. This gives us the $({\rm Pic}^+(X), \le^*)$ parametrized directed system $L'\mapsto -\otimes L'$. We claim that the projection $p_2:[{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+\to {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)$ induces a bijection
\[
{\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\rm Pic}^+(X)} [{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+\xymatrix{\ar[r]^{{\mathop{\rm colim}}\, p_2}_\sim&}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)
\]
First of all, as $X$ is quasi-projective, each $E\in {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)$ admits an $L\in {\rm Pic}^+(X)$ with $E\otimes L$ globally generated, so $p_2$ is surjective, hence ${\mathop{\rm colim}}\, p_2$ is also surjective. For injectivity, if two elements $(L, E)$, $(L', E')$ both go to the same element $E''\in {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)$, then $E=E'=E''$. Moreover, we have 
\[
(-\otimes L')(L, E)=(L\otimes L', E)=(-\otimes L)(L', E)
\]
so $(L,E)=(L',E)$ in the colimit. 

We factor the map 
\[
{\rm Hom}(X, {\mathbb P}^N\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M))\to {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X),\quad f\mapsto f^*(E_{m,M}(-1)),
\]
through  $p_2:[{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+\to {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)$ by sending $f$ to the pair
\[
((p_1\circ f)^*{\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^N}(1), f^*E_{m,M}(-1))\in [{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+.
\]


To conclude,  let $f:X\to {\mathbb P}^N\times{\mathbb P}^{N'}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M)$ be a morphism, and let $E=(p_{13}\circ f)^*(E_{m, M}(-1))$, $L=(p_1\circ f)^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^N}(1))$ and $L'=(p_2\circ f)^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^{N'}}(1))$. By construction, we have $E\otimes L=(p_3\circ f)^*(E_{m, M})$. We  have the map \eqref{Veronese2}
\[
\lambda_{N,N', ,M}:{\mathbb P}^N\times{\mathbb P}^{N'}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m,M)\to {\mathbb P}^{N''}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M'')
\]
with
\[
(p_1\circ \lambda_{N,N', ,M}\circ f)^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^{N''}}(1))= (\operatorname{Ver}_{N,N'}\circ f)^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^{N''}}(1))=L\otimes L',
\]
and by Lemma~\ref{lem:TensorIdentity}(1)
\[
(\lambda_{N,N', ,M}\circ f)^*(E_{m, M''}(-1))\cong (p_{13}\circ f)^*(E_{m, M}(-1)) = E.
\]
Thus we have 
\[
((p_1\circ f)^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^N}(1)), (p_{13}\circ f)^*(E_{m, M}(-1))=(L, E)\in {\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+
\]
and
\begin{multline*}
((p_1\circ\lambda_{N,N', ,M}\circ f)^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^{N''}}(1)),  (\lambda_{N,N', ,M}\circ f)^*(E_{m, M''}(-1))\\=(L\otimes L', E)\in [{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+.
\end{multline*}
This gives us
\begin{multline*}
(L\otimes L', E)= ((p_1\circ\lambda(X,m)(f))^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^{N''}}(1)),  \lambda(X,m)(f)^*(E_{m, M''}(-1))\\ = (-\otimes L')((p_1\circ f)^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^N}(1)), p_{13}(X)(f)^*(E_{m, M}(-1))\\=(-\otimes L')(L,E)\in [{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+.
\end{multline*}
Moreover, each such pair of elements $(L\otimes L', E)$, $(L, E)$ in  $[{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+$, $L, L'\in {\rm Pic}^+(X)$, arises in this way from some morphism 
\[
f:X\to {\mathbb P}^N\times{\mathbb P}^{N'}\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m, M).
\]
Thus, we have the identification
\[
{\operatorname{coeq}}(p_{13}(X), \lambda(X, m))\cong {\mathop{\rm colim}}_{{\rm Pic}^+(X)} [{\rm Pic}^+(X)\times {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^+\cong {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X),
\]
completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
Take $X\in {\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}_k^{{\operatorname{\text{\rm qp}}},{\operatorname{\text{\rm con}}}}$.   Then sending $(F, F')\in {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_{m}(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_{m'}(X)$ to   $[F]-[F']\in K_0(X)$ defines a bijection in  ${\mathbf{Sets}}_\bullet$. 
\[
\amalg_{m,m'\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_{m'}(X)/\sim_{K_0}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_0(X),
\]
natural in $X\in {\operatorname{\mathbf{Sch}}}_k^{{\operatorname{\text{\rm qp}}},{\operatorname{\text{\rm con}}}}$.
Here $K_0(X)$ is pointed by 0 and $\amalg_{m,m'\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_{m'}(X)/\sim_{K_0}$ is pointed by the class of $(0,0)\in {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_0(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_0(X)$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Note that $\amalg_{m\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)$ is a commutative monoid under direct sum.  If we restrict $\sim_{K_0}$ to the case of short exact sequences of the form $0\to E\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{\rm Id}}}E\to 0\to 0$, defining the equivalence relation $\sim_{\oplus}$, we see that sending $(F, F')\in {\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_{m'}(X)$ to the formal difference $F-F'$ in the group completion $[\amalg_{m\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^{\operatorname{gp}}$ gives a bijection of pointed sets
\begin{equation}\label{eqn:GpCompletionMap}
\amalg_{m,m'\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_{m'}(X)/\sim_{\oplus}\to [\amalg_{m\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^{\operatorname{gp}}.
\end{equation}
Also, as abelian groups, $[\amalg_{m\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)]^{\operatorname{gp}}$ is canonically isomorphic to $K_0^\oplus(X)$, defined as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes of locally free coherent sheaves on $X$, modulo the subgroup generated by  $\{[E\oplus E']-[E]-[E']\mid (E,E')\in  \amalg_{m,m'\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_{m'}(X)\}$.  

From this, we see that the map \eqref{eqn:GpCompletionMap}  passes to a bijection (in ${\mathbf{Sets}}_\bullet$) of
\[
\amalg_{m,m'\ge0}{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_m(X)\times{\operatorname{\bf Vec}}_{m'}(X)/\sim_{K_0}
\]
with the quotient (in the category ${\mathbf{Ab}}$)  of $K_0^\oplus(X)$ by the relation $[E']+[E'']\sim [E]$ for each  short exact sequence
\[
0\to E'\to E\to E''\to 0
\]
on $X$, which gives back the definition of $K_0(X)$.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:TwistedDirectSum} Let $E_1, E_2$ be locally free  sheaves on $X$ of rank $m_1$, $m_2$, $L_1$, $L_2$ globally generated invertible sheaves on $X$ such that $E_1\otimes L_1$ and $E_2\otimes L_2$ are globally generated. For $i=1,2$, let $g_i:X\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_i, M_i)$ be the morphism gotten by choosing $M_i$ generating global sections of $E_i\otimes L_i$,  let $\iota_i:X\to {\mathbb P}^{N_i}$ be the morphism gotten by choosing $N_i+1$ generating global sections of $L_i$,  let $f_i:=(\iota_i, g_i):X\to 
{\mathbb P}^{N_i}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_i, M_i)$ and let $m=m_1+m_2$. Then
\[
f_i^*(E_{m_i, M_i}(-1))\cong E_i,\ i=1,2,
\]
and
\[
(\widetilde{\oplus}\circ (f_1, f_2))^*(E_{m, M}(-1))\cong E_1\oplus E_2.
\]
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
We have already seen that $f_i^*(E_{m_i, M_i}(-1))\cong E_i$, and the second identity follows from this and \eqref{eqn:DirectSumPullback}.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:ExactSeqPresentation} Let $X$ be a quasi-projective $k$-scheme, let
 \[
E_\bullet:= 0\to E_s\to E_t\to E_q\to0
 \]
 be an exact sequence of locally free sheaves on $X$, with $E_s$ of rank $m_s$, $E_t$ of rank $m_t$ and $E_q$ of rank $m_q$. Let $L$ be a globally generated invertible sheaf on $X$ such that $E_t\otimes L$ is globally generated, and choose $M$ generating sections $s_1,\ldots, s_M$ of $E_t\otimes L$, giving the 
 corresponding morphism
 \[
 \phi:X\to {{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_t,m_q, M)
 \]
 with
 \[
 \phi^*(E_{m_\bullet, M})\cong E_\bullet\otimes L.
 \]
 Choosing $N+1$ generating global sections $t_0,\ldots, t_N$ for $L$ gives the morphism
 \[
 \iota:X\to {\mathbb P}^N 
 \]
 and the morphism
 \[
 \psi:=(\iota, \phi):X\to {\mathbb P}^N\times{{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet,M)
 \]
 with
 \[
 \psi^*(E_{m_\bullet, M}(-1))\cong E_\bullet.
 \]
 
 Let  $V$ be the $k$-vector space $k^M$ with basis $s_1,\ldots, s_M$, and choose $r\gg0$ so that \eqref{eqn:TwistConditions} for $(m_\bullet, M)$  holds.
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item Let $L_\phi=L\otimes \phi^*{\mathcal O}_{{{\mathcal F}{l}}}(r)$. Then  $E_?\otimes L_\phi$ is globally generated for $?=s,t,q$, and 
 \begin{equation}\label{eqn:PullbackIso}
  \phi^*(E_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{{\mathcal F}{l}}}(r))\cong E_\bullet\otimes L_\phi.
\end{equation}
 \item Mapping $H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M), E^?_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{{\mathcal F}{l}}}(r))$ to $H^0(X, E_?\otimes L_\phi)$ by the isomorphism \eqref{eqn:PullbackIso},  the image
 \[
 \phi^*(H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M), E^?_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{{\mathcal F}{l}}}(r)))\subset H^0(X, E_?\otimes L_\phi)
 \]
 generates $E_?\otimes L_\phi$.
 \item Our choice of isomorphism $H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M), E^?_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{{\mathcal F}{l}}}(r))\cong k^{M_?}$ gives rise to morphisms for $?=s,t,q$,
 \[
 \gamma_?:X\to {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_?, M_?)
 \]
 with $\gamma_?^*E_{m_?, M_?}\cong E_?\otimes L_\phi$ and with
 \[
 \gamma_?=g_?\circ  \phi.
 \]
 \item Let $W=\oplus_{i=0}^Nk\cdot t_i$, and let $W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}:=H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M), {\mathcal O}_{{{\mathcal F}{l}}}(r))$. Map $W\otimes W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}$  to $H^0(X, L_\phi)$ via the definition of $L_\phi$ as $L\otimes \phi^*{\mathcal O}_{{{\mathcal F}{l}}}(r)$ together with the evident map $W\to H^0(X, L)$. Then the image of 
 $W\otimes W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}$ in $H^0(X, L_\phi)$ generates $L_\phi$, giving the morphism
 \[
 \operatorname{Ver}_{W, W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}}:X\to {\mathbb P}^{N^*},\ N^*=(N+1)\cdot{\operatorname{\rm dim}}_kW_{{\mathcal F}{l}},
 \]
and, after a suitable choice of basis for $W$, $W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}$  and $W\otimes W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}$, we have
\[
(\operatorname{Ver}_{W,W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}}, \gamma_?)=\Lambda_?\circ \psi,\ ?=s,t,q.
\]
\item We have isomorphisms
\[
(\operatorname{Ver}_{W,W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}}, \gamma_?)^*(E_{m_?, M_?}(-1))\cong E_?,\ ?=s,t,q.
\]
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
For (1),  we have  
 \[
 \phi^*(E_{m_\bullet,M})\cong E_\bullet\otimes L
 \]
 by construction, and thus $\phi^*(E_{m_\bullet,M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r))\cong E_\bullet\otimes L_\phi$. Since $E^?_{m_\bullet,M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r)$ is globally generated for $?=s,t,q$, so are the $E_?\otimes L_\phi$.
 
 For (2), this follows from (1), since a space of global generators for $E^?_{m_\bullet,M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r)$ pulls back via $\phi$ to a space of global generators for $\phi^*(E^?_{m_\bullet,M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r))$.
 
 For (3), the map $g_?$ classifies the surjection
 \[
\pi: H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}, E^?_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r))\otimes_k{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}\to E^?_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r)
 \]
 after a choice of isomorphism $H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}, E^?_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r))\cong k^{M_?}$ and thus $g_?\circ \phi$ classifies the surjection
 \begin{equation}\label{eqn:PiSurjection}
k^{M_?}\otimes_k{\mathcal O}_X\cong  H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}, E^?_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r))\otimes_k{\mathcal O}_X\to \phi^*(E^?_{m_\bullet, M}\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r))\cong E_?\otimes L_\phi
 \end{equation}
 induced by $\pi$ and the isomorphism from (1). As \eqref{eqn:PiSurjection} is the surjection used to define $\gamma_?$, we have
 \[
 \gamma_?=g_?\circ\phi,
 \]
 and
 \[
 \gamma_?^*(E^?_{m_\bullet, M})\cong  E_?\otimes L_\phi,\ ?=s,t,q.
 \]
 
 For (4), we have
 \[
 \Lambda_?\circ \psi=(\operatorname{Ver}_{N, N(m_\bullet, M,r)}\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{\operatorname{\rm Gr}})\circ({\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^N}\times (i_{m_\bullet, M,r}, g_?))\circ(\iota,\phi).
 \]
 so
 \[
 p_2\circ(\Lambda_?\circ \psi)=g_?\circ \phi=\gamma_?.
 \]
 Moreover, the composition $i_{m_\bullet, M,r}\circ\phi:X\to {\mathbb P}^{N(m_\bullet, M)}$ classifies the surjection
\[
k^{N(m_\bullet, M,r)+1}\otimes{\mathcal O}_X\cong H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}, {\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r))\otimes{\mathcal O}_X\to \phi^*{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r),
\]
induced by the canonical surjection $H^0({{\mathcal F}{l}}, {\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r))\otimes{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}\to {\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r)$, after pulling back by $\phi$. Thus, the composition
\[
X\xrightarrow{(\iota, \phi)}{\mathbb P}^N\times{{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M)\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{\rm Id}}_{{\mathbb P}^N}\times i_{m_\bullet, M,r}}
{\mathbb P}^N\times {\mathbb P}^{N(m_\bullet, M,r)}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ver}_{N, N(m_\bullet, M,r)}}{\mathbb P}^{N^*}
\]
is the map classifying the surjection
\begin{multline*}
k^{N^*+1}\otimes{\mathcal O}_X\cong k^{N+1}\otimes k^{N(m_\bullet, M,r)+1}\otimes{\mathcal O}_X\\
\cong W\otimes W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}\otimes{\mathcal O}_X\to L\otimes\phi^*{\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal F}{l}}(r)=L_\phi
\end{multline*}
which, up to suitable choice of bases, is exactly the map $\operatorname{Ver}_{W, W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}}$. Thus
\[
p_1\circ (\Lambda_?\circ \psi)=\operatorname{Ver}_{W, W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}}
\]
so
\[
\Lambda_?\circ \psi=(\operatorname{Ver}_{W, W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}}, \gamma_?)
\]
as claimed. 

For point (5), 
\begin{align*}
(\operatorname{Ver}_{W,W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}}, \gamma_?)^*(E_{m_?, M_?}(-1))&= \gamma_?^*(E_{m_?, M_?})\otimes\operatorname{Ver}_{W,W_{{\mathcal F}{l}}}^*({\mathcal O}_{{\mathbb P}^{N^*}}(-1))\\
&=E_?\otimes L_\phi\otimes L_\phi^{-1}=E_?.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
\label{def:TotalAndSum} Given integers $N, N_1, N_2$, $m_\bullet:=(m_t, m_q)$, $M$, $m_1, M_1$, choose $r$ satisfying \eqref{eqn:TwistConditions} for $(m_\bullet, M)$, and let  $M_t^*:=M_t\cdot(N(m_\bullet, M,r)+1)$,  $N^*_i=(N(m_\bullet, M,r)+1)(N_i+1)-1$,  $M_i^*:=M_1\cdot (N_i+1)$, $i=1,2$; see \eqref{eqn:ChosenSurjections} for the definition of $M_t$.\\[5pt]
1. Define
\[
\oplus(s+q,1):{\mathbb P}^N\times {{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M)\times({\mathbb P}^{N_1}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_1, M_1)) \to {\mathbb P}^{N^*_1}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_t+m_1, M_t^*+M_1^*)
\]
be the composition
\begin{multline*}
({\mathbb P}^N\times {{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M))\times({\mathbb P}^{N_1}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_1, M_1))\xrightarrow{\Lambda_{s+q}\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}}
{\mathbb P}^{N^*}\times  {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_t, M_t)\times {\mathbb P}^{N_1}\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_1, M_1)\\
\xrightarrow{\tilde{\oplus}}
{\mathbb P}^{N_1^*}\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_t+m_1, M_t^*+M_1^*)
\end{multline*}
2. Define
\[
\oplus(t,2):{\mathbb P}^N\times {{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M)\times({\mathbb P}^{N_2}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_2, M_2)) \to {\mathbb P}^{N^*_2}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_t+m_2, M_t^*+M_2^*)
\]
as the composition
\begin{multline*}
{\mathbb P}^N\times {{\mathcal F}{l}}(m_\bullet, M)\times({\mathbb P}^{N_2}\times{\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_2, M_2))\xrightarrow{\Lambda_t\times{\operatorname{\rm Id}}}
{\mathbb P}^{N^*}\times  {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_t, M_t)\times {\mathbb P}^{N_2}\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_2, M_2)\\
\xrightarrow{\tilde{\oplus}}
{\mathbb P}^{N_2^*}\times {\operatorname{\rm Gr}}(m_t+m_2, M_t^*+M_2^*).
\end{multline*}
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
As the reader will see in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:K0Presentation}, the choice of $r$ in the definition of the maps
$\oplus(s+q,1)$ and  $\oplus(t,2)$ does not matter in our presentation of $K_0(X)$, and so we have not included this choice in the notation for these maps, even though this choice does enter into the definition of the numbers $M_?, M_?^*, M_i^*, N_i^*$, $?=s,t,q$, $i=1,2$.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:K0Presentation} Let $X$ be a connected quasi-projective scheme over a field $k$. Let 
\[
